newsitem.title: USA: Calif. home prices climb 3.5 pct in May - survey.
newsitem.headline: Calif. home prices climb 3.5 pct in May - survey.

text.p: Home prices in California climbed 3.5 percent in May, the largest annual increase in more than five years, according to a survey released on Wednesday.
The California Association of Realtors said the median price of a single-family home was $185,360, up from $179,100 recorded in May last year.
The largest increases were reported in Palm Springs, San Diego, Santa Barbara, Orange County, Los Angeles and in the Ventura area, the association said.

"After lagging behind the northern section of the state for so long, it is very gratifying to see noteworthy price appreciation finally reach southern California," association president Bob Kulick said in a statement.

The pace of California home resale activity also accelerated during the month. Closed escrow sales in May were 544,690, a 2.9 percent boost over May 1996 when 529,540 homes were sold, the association said.
